key_insight: JEPA-Anything proposes a single, domain-agnostic way to learn predictive world models across very different systems. Its core idea is to factor predictions into orthogonal components so the model can capture complementary aspects of the future more effectively.
problem_solved: Most predictive world models work well only within a specific domain, such as vision, robotics, or simulation. This paper tackles the challenge of building one learning principle that can generalize across radically different worlds.
method: Extends joint-embedding predictive architectures with orthogonal predictive factorization (OPF).
Decomposes latent targets into complementary factors and predicts them with dedicated pathways.
Learns a shared predictive framework intended to transfer across diverse domains without relying on domain-specific modeling rules.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a path toward reusable predictive models that can work across multiple domains with less manual redesign. It could simplify world-model training and improve generalization in agents that need to reason, plan, or act in unfamiliar environments.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing input world states -> latent factors -> orthogonal prediction branches -> reconstructed future representation.
A split-factor illustration highlighting complementary latent components and their interactions.
A comparison chart of domain-specific world models vs. JEPA-Anything across different tasks or worlds.
Icons representing different domains (robotics, video, physics, games) connected to one shared framework.
paper_title: JEPA-Anything: Learning Predictive Models across Different Worlds
paper_authors: Taoyong Cui, Zhongyao Wang, Xinyue Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhaochen Yu
